stories.title: Human lung chip models macrophage-amplified viral injury and mechanical overdistension
stories.takeaway: A human lung-chip study models interactions among infection, macrophages, mechanical stress and secondary bacterial infection.
stories.what_happened: Published November 19 in Nature Communications, the study uses a human lung chip to investigate macrophage-exacerbated viral injury and mechanically driven bacterial superinfection.
stories.why_it_matters: Illustrates how controlled mechanical and immune inputs in organ chips can help separate contributors to respiratory injury.
stories.caveat: An in vitro lung model cannot establish patient-level clinical effects; full experimental detail was not independently accessible.

stories.title: Fermentable fiber, colonic acidity and GPR65 signaling in blood-pressure control
stories.takeaway: A study links microbial fiber fermentation, intestinal pH and proton sensing to experimental blood-pressure regulation.
stories.what_happened: Published November 20, the study combines human genetic associations with mouse resistant-starch experiments and reports GPR65-associated signaling and inflammatory changes.
stories.why_it_matters: Provides a mechanistic connection between microbial metabolites, intestinal physiology and systemic cardiovascular biology.
stories.caveat: Mouse mechanistic effects and genetic associations do not establish an effective dietary hypertension treatment in humans.

stories.title: Blautia and circulating butyrate associated with IgA nephropathy
stories.takeaway: A multicenter cross-sectional analysis reports gut microbial and metabolic signatures in kidney disease.
stories.what_happened: Published November 20 in Scientific Reports, investigators profiled fecal 16S data from 187 participants and a separate 142-person replication cohort, focusing on Blautia and butyrate.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows the potential for cross-organ microbiome studies to connect mucosal biology with systemic disease.
stories.caveat: Cross-sectional associations cannot determine causality or validate a microbiome-directed treatment.

stories.title: Synthetic antigen-presenting cell viscoelasticity influences T-cell metabolism
stories.takeaway: A synthetic-cell platform independently varies mechanical relaxation to probe immune-cell activation.
stories.what_happened: Published November 20 in Nature Communications, researchers describe SynVAC artificial antigen-presenting cells with tunable stress relaxation independent of stiffness and ligand density.
stories.why_it_matters: An example of biomaterial mechanobiology informing cell manufacturing and engineered immune therapies.
stories.caveat: The accessible abstract does not establish comparative clinical outcomes or long-term manufacturing scalability.

stories.title: Norovirus capsid flexibility revealed by asymmetric antibody binding
stories.takeaway: Structural work shows that antibody interactions can expose flexibility in the human norovirus capsid.
stories.what_happened: Published November 19 in Nature Communications, the study examines symmetry-breaking antibody binding and capsid malleability in pandemic human norovirus.
stories.why_it_matters: Could inform interpretation of viral antigenicity and design of antiviral antibodies or vaccines.
stories.caveat: Structural findings alone do not demonstrate protection or vaccine efficacy in people.
